Nirvana

nir-VAH-nuh -- three syllables, stress on the second syllable, VAH. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Nirvana is a state of happiness and peace.

With the twins finally asleep, the quiet porch felt like nirvana to their exhausted parents.

Worked Example

All winter, the gardener shovels snow and scrapes ice. But inside the greenhouse it is seventy degrees and silent -- tomatoes ripening in January, the only sound a slow drip of water -- and every worry stays outside the glass door.

For the gardener, that greenhouse is nirvana: a state of happiness and peace so complete that troubles cannot seem to reach it. In everyday English, nirvana names the perfect peace itself, wherever you find it.

How Nirvana Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

paradise

paradise: a place or state of perfect happiness

serenity

serenity: deep, untroubled calm

Antonyms

torment

torment: great suffering or distress

agony

agony: extreme pain of body or mind

How Strong Is It? — serenity → nirvana → paradise

serenity vs. nirvana

serenity vs. nirvana: Serenity is the calm half only -- still water, no waves -- while nirvana adds happiness to the peace: nothing hurts AND nothing is missing.

paradise vs. nirvana

paradise vs. nirvana: Paradise is the strongest match: both name a perfect state, but paradise pictures a perfect PLACE, while nirvana names the perfect inner STATE you carry with you.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — nir-

prefix — nir-: out, away (Sanskrit)

root — va-

root — va-: to blow (Sanskrit vati)

suffix — -na

suffix — -na: Sanskrit ending: 'having been' (Sanskrit)

Put it together

Put it together: Nirvana is Sanskrit for 'a blowing out,' like a candle flame: nir- ('out') plus va ('to blow') plus the -na ending meaning 'having been' -- in Buddhism it names the blowing out of all suffering and craving. Everyday English borrowed the afterglow: a state of deep happiness and peace.

Use the root in a new word: nirvanic

Use the root in a new word: nirvanic: Fans described the choir's final chord as almost nirvanic.

Word Building

Word Choice

In Buddhism, capital-N Nirvana is the ultimate release from suffering; in everyday English, lowercase nirvana is any state of perfect happiness and peace -- a hammock, a quiet cove, a greenhouse in January. Note the pace: euphoria races, but nirvana rests. If the joy is loud and electric, it is not nirvana.
